bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for smelter and alumina expansion; no dividend guidance mentioned; retained earnings funding capex; JV with Neyveli Lignite to share 50% of power plant capex
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Alumina price volatility ($300-310 expected FY27); Middle East export disruption; caustic soda and fuel cost inflation; pay commission impact (10-15% employee cost rise from Jan27); smelter commissioning delays
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic on volume growth and cost control; transparent on pricing (LME-linked, no hedging); proactive on captive resources and JV partnerships; acknowledges alumina oversupply but sees bottoming; dismisses Utkarsh JV as uneconomic
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Red mud is a future rare earth/gallium source (pilot stage); 10% of coal via E-auction despite higher cost; domestic alumina sales grew 250% YoY to 1.4LMT; special grade alumina production minimal (15-20KMT); royalty is LME-linked at 0.56% of value, not fixed
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- One of the largest integrated Bauxite-Alumina-Aluminium-Power complexes in the country - mine, refinery, smelter and captive power in one chain
- Bauxite supply secured from captive Panchpatmali mines with all statutory clearances, lease validity to 16.11.2032 (Central & North Block) and 19.07.2029 (South Block)
- Energy security from a 1,200 MW captive power plant, a Fuel Supply Agreement with MCL for 47.16 lakh MT of coal for CPP Units 1-8, and captive Utkal-D&E coal blocks that supplied 40 lakh MT to the CPP in FY 2025-26
- Caustic soda, the other critical refinery raw material, securitised through the GNAL joint venture with GACL under a long-term agreement for up to 1,50,000 DMT per annum
- Dedicated bulk shipment facility at Visakhapatnam for alumina exports, with 15,000 DMT caustic soda storage
- 198 MW of wind power projects and 1,060 kWp rooftop solar reduce dependence on coal-based captive generation
- Record FY 2025-26 physical performance - highest-ever bauxite excavation, alumina hydrate, calcined alumina and cast metal production, with production beyond rated capacities across major operating units
- Rated 'Very Good' under the MoU signed with the Government of India for FY 2024-25
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Energy intensity and coal dependence of aluminium smelting — Power consumption constitutes a major portion of production cost and dependence on coal-based captive power increases exposure to fuel cost volatility and environmental regulations. The MD&A calls smelting in India 'highly energy intensive and coal dependent' a perennial weakness given limited coal reserves, and flags non-competitive energy prices and inconsistent coal linkage for the non-power sector as hits to cost competitiveness.
- Carbon pricing and border adjustment regimes (EU-CBAM, India-CCTS) — Aluminium production with thermal power is highly energy-intensive and emerging carbon regulations such as CCTS and CBAM increase compliance risk. The MD&A states the differential carbon tax is expected to impact the competitiveness of Indian-produced aluminium and products in overseas markets - material for a company that exported 27% of turnover to 11 countries - with tariff costs (US) and compliance costs adding further pressure.
- Commodity price and exchange-rate volatility — The Company is exposed to commodity price volatility, regulatory change, operational disruption and strategic risk, mitigated through an ERM framework, regular risk assessment and hedging strategies where applicable. The MD&A notes alumina prices trending down and expected to stay subdued in a $300-315/tonne range on structural surplus, and lists fluctuations in global prices/exchange rates among perpetual threats.
- Red mud and ash waste management — Alumina refining and thermal power generation generate significant quantities of red mud and ash requiring safe storage and disposal, under increasing regulatory scrutiny; negative financial implication from capex and operational costs for storage, handling and compliance, offset by potential by-product revenue and reduced long-term liability.
- Water availability and water-intensive operations — Aluminium refining and thermal power generation are water-intensive, with increased regulatory oversight and competition for water resources in operational regions; mitigation is closed-loop water systems, zero liquid discharge, recycling and reuse, and rainwater harvesting across plants and mines.
- Biodiversity, land use and mining licence to operate — Mining activities may impact land use, forests and biodiversity, especially in sensitive ecological zones, leading to adverse reactions; mitigated by progressive mine closure plans, land reclamation and afforestation, biodiversity conservation and adherence to environmental clearance conditions. Community relations are separately identified as material, since social acceptance is crucial for uninterrupted operations and project expansions.
- Occupational health and safety — Operations involve significant safety risks including exposure to hazardous conditions, which could result in injuries, fatalities and productivity loss; mitigated by safety management systems, training, digital safety monitoring and continuous audits.
- Logistics bottlenecks and import competition — Lack of a reliable coordinated multimodal logistics network raises costs, extends lead times and causes port congestion, working-capital lock-in and delays in raw material inflows and finished goods outflows, limiting export competitiveness. Alongside this, rising imports of value-added products and cheaper aluminium imports through FTA routes pressure domestic market share in downstream segments.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Navratna CPSE with Government of India holding 51.28%; described as an 'Integrated Bauxite-Alumina-Aluminium-Power-Coal Complex'.
- Deck claims NALCO is a 'Global leader in producing bauxite and alumina at the lowest cost.'
- Asset chain spans captive bauxite mines (Damanjodi), alumina refinery (Damanjodi), aluminium smelter (Angul), captive power plant (Angul), coal, wind power and dedicated port facilities for storage of alumina, caustic soda and ship loading.
- On the demand backdrop the deck states India 'is expected to remain one of the fastest-growing Aluminium markets globally, with domestic Aluminium demand projected to grow at around 6-8% CAGR through 2030.'
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] The deck lists 10 Board Level Committees but states that 'Due to absence of Independent Directors on the Board w.e.f. 01.04.2026, no Board level Committees are in position' - a live board-composition gap.
- [Governance] 'Excellent' rating in the FY25-26 self-appraisal reports to the DPE, plus 17 core policies and guidelines and regular risk assessments.
- [Price outlook] The deck's LME aluminium price outlook for CY 2026 is 'expected to average between US$ ~3200-3300/T', with global inventories at historically low levels (0.26 Mln. T) and the market 'still expected to be in deficit during the H2-2026 before gradually moving towards a more balanced position in 2027'.
- [Price drivers] Named swing factors include Middle East production/logistics disruption, moderation of the 'war-risk' premium, US tariff incentives for domestic aluminium, renewable/auto/infrastructure demand, the US$ and Fed stance, and increased Chinese (>222%) and Indonesian exports alleviating supply tightness.
- [Demand mix] Indian aluminium consumption split as given: Electrical 48%, Transportation & Automobile 15%, Building & Construction 13%, Consumer Durables 7%, Machinery & Equipments 7%, Packaging 4%, Others 6%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: NALCO mines bauxite at Panchpatmali, refines it into alumina and hydrate at Damanjodi and smelts primary aluminium at Anugola, Odisha, on power from its own 1,200 MW coal-fired captive plant fed partly by the captive Utkal-D&E coal blocks. Its two reported businesses are Chemicals (alumina) and Metal (aluminium); per the BRSR, aluminium products contributed 73% and alumina products 27% of turnover in FY 2025-26. Alumina and aluminium are sold to domestic customers through Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) agreements and by participating in tenders across 23 states, while international customers, in 11 countries, are served through online global tenders; exports were 27% of turnover.

- **Metal (Aluminium):** Aluminium products (NIC 242005), Aluminium cast metal

- GACL-NALCO Alkalies & Chemicals Private Limited — JV: Associate (Joint Venture), 40% of shares held by the listed entity; a JV of National Aluminium Company Limited and Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited. outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Growth through brownfield expansion in the core business: 1 Million Tonne 5th Stream at the Damanjodi alumina refinery, and a planned 0.5 Million Tonne brownfield expansion of the smelter with an associated power plant.
- Backward integration for raw-material security: captive Panchpatmali bauxite, development of the Pottangi bauxite mine through an appointed MDO, operation of the Utkal-D&E captive coal blocks (being augmented from 40 to 48 lakh tonnes per annum), and caustic soda from the GNAL joint venture with GACL.
- Forward integration and downstream value addition through the Angul Aluminium Park JV with IDCO, aimed at enhancing domestic aluminium consumption and generating employment.
- Selective diversification into critical minerals overseas through the KABIL JV with Hindustan Copper and MECL, including lithium resources in Argentina, aligned with India's critical-mineral security objective.
- Captive power expansion in JV mode: a 50:50 JV with NLCIL for a 4x270 MW (1080 MW) thermal captive power plant at Anugola, plus exploration of 200-250 MW of firm renewable energy (RE-RTC).
- Decarbonisation through renewable energy integration - 198 MW of wind, rooftop solar, RE imports and wheeling from own wind plants - and by backing down coal-based captive generation using 150 MW of RE drawn from GRIDCO during solar hours.
- Corporate Plan structured as a 3-year action plan, 7-year strategy and 15-year vision to improve top line and bottom line and overcome the commodity cycle, operationalised through the Annual Business Plan as the year's roadmap of physical and financial targets.
- Strengthening governance: Board approval of an Anti-Bribery Management System (ABMS) aligned with ISO 37001.
- Continued MSE development, including procurement through the GeM portal and the NAMASYA app, with special focus on women-owned and SC/ST-owned MSEs.
- Reasonable Assurance on BRSR CORE for FY 2025-26 obtained from TUV SUD South Asia Pvt. Ltd., on a standalone reporting boundary.
- GHG: transition toward renewable energy sourcing, improvement in energy efficiency, deployment of emission reduction technologies, and development of low-carbon aluminium products aligned with global standards.
- Renewable capacity: 198.40 MW of wind power plants established across various states, being augmented to 213.40 MW with a 15 MW project at Kayathar, Tamil Nadu.
- Water: implementation of closed-loop water systems, zero liquid discharge mechanisms, recycling and reuse initiatives, and rainwater harvesting structures across plants and mines.
- Waste: adoption of red mud and ash utilisation initiatives, strengthening of waste handling systems, proper disposal practices, and collaboration with research institutions for recovery.
- Air quality: installation and upgradation of emission control equipment such as Electrostatic Precipitators, fluorine absorption systems and continuous emission monitoring.
- Biodiversity: progressive mine closure plans, land reclamation and afforestation programmes, biodiversity conservation initiatives and adherence to environmental clearance conditions.
- Governance: Enterprise Risk Management framework with a Board-level Risk Management Committee that reviews exceptional risk reports, risk registers maintained by nominated risk officers and overviewed by Internal Auditors; business ethics upheld through code of conduct, vigilance mechanisms, internal audits, whistleblower policies and compliance monitoring.
- Social: compliance with presidential directives on SC/ST/OBC/EWS, PWD and Ex-Servicemen reservation - manpower of 4,864 as on 31 March 2026 including 342 women, 739 SC (15.19%), 916 ST (18.83%), 998 OBC (20.51%), 99 PWD (2.04%), 34 EWS (0.69%) and 10 Ex-Servicemen; zero man-days lost due to labour disputes in FY 2025-26.

outlook.body: NALCO's expansion programme is a brownfield build-out of the existing bauxite-alumina-aluminium-power chain. The 5th Stream of the Alumina Refinery at Damanjodi will add 1.0 MTPY to the existing installed capacity of 2.1 MTPY at a projected expenditure of Rs 5,677.4 crore, using improved Medium Pressure Digestion technology of M/s. Rio Tinto Alcan Limited; Environmental Clearance from MoEF & CC and Consent to Establish from the Odisha State Pollution Control Board are in hand, detailed engineering, procurement and site work are complete, phase-wise trial and testing commenced from June 2026, and production is to be stabilised in H2 2026-27. Bauxite for the 5th Stream is envisaged from the Pottangi Mines - mining lease executed, all statutory clearances in place and an MDO appointed on 09 December 2025 for 25 years, with operationalisation planned in Q3 FY 2026-27 and production expected from Q4 FY 2026-27 - with an alternative route through a crushing & conveying system at the existing Panchpatmali South Block at an estimated capital outlay of Rs 496 crore, about 93% physically complete till 31 May 2026 and scheduled to be operationalised by October 2026. In power, the Company is adding a 15 MW wind project at Kayathar, Tamil Nadu at a capital expenditure of Rs 120 crore, taking wind capacity from 198.40 MW to 213.40 MW, with 4 WTGs likely to be commissioned in Q2 FY 2026-27 and the balance 6 progressively by Q3 FY 2026-27; an aggregate 7,000 kWp of rooftop solar is planned for implementation during 2026-27. The combined Utkal-D&E captive coal mine produced 4 MT in FY 2025-26 and 4.8 MT is planned for FY 2026-27. The next phase is a brownfield aluminium smelter expansion of approximately 0.5 Million TPA at Anugola - DPR in progress, preliminary study report covering a two-phase expansion prepared, technology licensor selection under finalisation, EC public hearing concluded and land acquisition through IDCO under way - supported by a 4x270 MW thermal captive power plant inside the existing CPP premises, to be developed in JV mode with NLCIL (JV agreement signed, JV company formation at an advanced stage) which will also supply renewable energy. Raw-material and downstream positions are held through joint ventures: GNAL with GACL (2.7 lakh TPA caustic soda plant with 130 MW CPP at Dahej, supplying NALCO's refinery), Angul Aluminium Park with IDCO for downstream conductors, extrusions, castings and foils, KABIL with HCL and MECL for overseas lithium and cobalt assets, and UADNL with MIDHANI (a proposed 60,000 TPA high-end aluminium alloy plant found commercially unviable, with the Ministry of Mines having directed winding up of the project). The Corporate Plan frames this as a 3-year action plan, 7-year strategy and 15-year vision. On a standalone basis the Company achieved a capex of Rs 2,068.16 crore in FY 2025-26; the Director (Projects & Technical)'s profile additionally refers to brownfield projects involving an investment of around Rs 30,000 crore.

outlook.body:
- Global aluminium market expected to grow at approximately 4.5% CAGR during 2026-2033, driven by automotive, solar power, construction, packaging and electrical end-uses.
- The aluminium industry is expected to remain in structural deficit in 2026, with the margin of deficit dependent on Middle-East curtailments and capacity-expansion timelines.
- China's production ceiling of 45 Million TPA lags its consumption need of 46 Million TPA, making it a net importer; consumption in the rest of Asia is expected to remain robust in 2026.
- Alumina prices are expected to stay subdued within a $300-315/tonne range on average as incremental capacity from Asia and other regions keeps the market well-supplied; the structural surplus is expected to dominate.
- Average aluminium price in FY 2025-26 was $2,772/tonne against $2,526/tonne the previous year, on China's capacity ceiling, tariffs, CBAM in Europe, low exchange inventories and Middle-East curtailments; 2026 is framed as a year of 'Great Rebalancing' marked by a 'Supply driven Market Shift'.
- Bauxite price outlook remains bearish through 2026 on higher Guinea production and risks to Chinese bauxite consumption tied to the smelting production cap.
- India's total aluminium consumption reached ~6.12 Million MT in FY 2025-26, up 11.4%, while domestic production grew 1.4% to 4.3 Million MT and exports declined 5.9% - indicating robust domestic demand.
- Indian aluminium market expected to grow at a CAGR of around 6.2%-7.8% till 2030 on consensus forecast; India's domestic demand expected to rise from 6.2 Million Tonnes in 2025-26 to 8.0-8.5 Million Tonnes by 2030.
- India's per capita aluminium consumption of 3.4 kg against a world average of 12 kg indicates immense consumption potential, supported by GoI investment in infrastructure, railways, airports, renewables and automobiles.
- Demand pull from the energy transition - EV light-weighting (GoI targeting 30% EV penetration by 2030), solar panel frames, wind turbine components, grid upgrades, 5G and AI data-centre extrusions/billets.
- Cost and competitiveness headwinds: energy-intensive coal-dependent smelting, carbon pricing (EU-CBAM, India-CCTS) expected to hit the competitiveness of Indian aluminium overseas, non-competitive energy prices and inconsistent coal linkage, and fragmented multimodal logistics raising costs and lock-in.
- Domestic market-share pressure from rising imports of value-added products and cheaper aluminium imports through FTA routes.
